1bnpo8d.46: The symbol of the village, overlooking two valleys.
1fnaqdb.238: The village is enclosed by a medieval wall of elliptical shape with square towers and the gateway called Aretina, connected to the fortress. Inside the Palazzo Pretorio of the fourteenth century and, in Piazza Lazzeri, a medieval cistern.
18qkj4m.48: A medieval village still closed in its walls.
c420p.136: Romanesque church dating back to the year 1000, then enlarged and renovated, and rebuilt after the bombings of the Second World War.
6e1uvf.41: The Romanesque church reborn after the war.
1ijie3l.150: At the Sinese Gate, another entrance to the castle, a sixteenth-century tabernacle in polychrome majolica of the Robbiana workshop with the Madonna and Child.

1my8o3w.130: A place reminiscent of the massacre of World War II in which 244 people were killed, along with a tombstone and a monument.

faylaw.36: Birdwatching and walking along the Arno.

15nn3ec.446: The center of the new land founded in 1299, first called San Giovanni in Altura and then Castel San Giovanni: a large square divided into two, Piazza Masaccio and Piazza Cavour, around the Palazzo d'Arnolfo, and Corso Italia flanked by medieval and Renaissance buildings. 1wihsmd.44: The double square of a founding city.
xnbw1t.628: Built between two and fourteenth century between the two squares, it housed the representative of the Florentine municipality and the town council, with rooms for wheat in case of war or famine; the works of the first fifteenth century for the apartments of the vicar marked the role of St. John in the Valdarno. Portici, crenellated tower and about 250 coats of arms of the vicars on the façade, from the first fifteenth century to 1772; in the atrium frescoes and coats of arms of the fifteenth century and the Marzocco. 13n0sa5.57: The facade with 250 coats of arms and the history of new cities.

1xbj72n.488: Small museum of sacred art in the premises next to the basilica, with paintings, sculptures, furnishings and vestments from the late fourteenth to the eighteenth century coming from churches and convents of the territory. The masterpiece is the Annunciation of Blessed Angelico (1432-1440); there are works of Scheggia, brother of Masaccio, already in San Lorenzo, Mariotto di Cristofano, Jacopo del Sellaio, Domenico di Michelino, Giovanni da San Giovanni and the triptych of the Trinity between Saints of Mariotto of Nardo from the Pieve.
24uvz6.35: The Annunciation of the Angelic Blessed.
1uplas5.536: According to Ugo Procacci's archive research, Masaccio spent most of his childhood there (it is not the established birthplace). 12dxhpw.50: Contemporary art in the house of Masaccio child.
h2y5pc.492: Gothic church of the fourteenth century on the side of Piazza Masaccio, which incorporated a smaller church as a right aisle; sandstone and brick facade. 1p2p5q7.293: The baptismal church of the city, begun in 1312 next to the disappearance Porta Sant'Andrea, in front of the Palazzo d'Arnolfo: classic façade with pediment and three arched porch on Tuscan columns decorated with rounds of Robbiana school, inside with a single nave with wooden cover.
g32afz.42: The fourteenth-century parish church in front of the palace.
1fbwrk2.406: Part of a complex that was a hospital of the community until the early sixteenth century and around 1528 became a monastery of Augustinian nuns; a small late Baroque church, renovated in the second half of the seventeenth century, with stuccoes, two canvases and the fresco of the ceiling of the Florentine Antonio Puglieschi, high altar of 1685 and a Madonna with Child attributed to the Master of the Nativity of Castello (about 1460).
md64t7.50: A table of the Master of the Nativity of Castello.

1x9glci.40: The dish of the city, with its stake.

1ajevdz.36: The crenellated tower reflected in the Arno.
1qsbvny.298: Built in the thirteenth century to replace the first church of the castle, considered too small, it was renovated from the end of the seventeenth century, when the loggia was added to the façade; the bell tower is from the nineteenth century and the current appearance dates back to the second post-war period. 1m9s93m.39: The religious heart of the village on the Arno.

15udl2e.46: Etruscan and Middle Ages of Casentino in two rooms.
1h4fyjo.500: Castello documented from the 11th century, of the Ubertini and then divided with the monks of Camaldoli, submitted to Florence in 1386; from 1870 the Bastogi family had it rebuilt in neo-Gothic and neo-romantic style by an architect who had worked in Brolio. 96lpo4.54: A neo-Medieval castle above the valley of the river Talla.

48tnkf.46: The Castle of the Flowers on the Arno valley.

It preserves two cycles of frescoes: one of about 1370-1380 attributed to the Master of Pieve in Sietina and one of the nineties of the fifteenth century, of followers of Lorentino d'Andrea influenced by Piero della Francesca, commissioned by the family of merchants Bacci Arezzo.
w6sjf0.89: A Romanesque church on the Arno with Gothic and Renaissance frescoes from Piero's school.
1qdrdv1.283: Documented from the 10th century, in the center of the village of San Giovanni, owes its current appearance especially to the changes of the eighteenth century and preserves a crucifix of the fourteenth century. sp700k.59: A fourteenth-century crucifix and a great view of the valley.

1wuroz9.55: One of the oldest documented parishes in the territory.

1mo5jfo.48: A village still closed by its medieval walls.
p73yyd.135: Small village with medieval buildings that have remained unchanged, indicated by Visit Tuscany as a stop in the territory of Capolona.
1xcmdj6.35: A medieval village as it was.

11f1rj7.60: The ancient capital, with the Portaccia of the castle on the Arno.

1gsma6d.51: A castle in Casentino between tower, loggia and coats of arms.

7hwba4.70: The peasant and pastoral civilization of Casentino in a medieval tower.
ck1mlx.85: Temporarily closed according to Visit Tuscany; check with the Casentino Ecomuseum

1qkk58y.48: The castle of the bishop-warriors of Campaldino.

zy5i5y.299: Itinerary in the woods along the Rio stream leading to one of the major ancient sites of production of gunpowder, obtained by mixing sulphur and salter; along the path the "pillo" is a hole in the sandstone used as a mortar, and the "mazzapicchio" is a wooden instrument moved by the force of water.
1f5nh85.48: On the trail of the illegal gunpowder.
1dlwcx4.391: Ferruginous and sulphurous waters already known in ancient times, as shown by the votive bronze found in the surroundings, frequented by the pilgrims of the Via Romea in the Middle Ages and valued by the Ubertini in the seventeenth century. 1j5uiy4.139: Church of the XVII century consecrated in 1614 by Pier Francesco Ubertini; the bell tower with the clock is of the mid-nineteenth century.
flo0zp.32: The church wanted by the Ubertini.

1h57bvt.43: The palace of the popes and the granddukes guests.

1tx4h00.37: The Medici sign in the middle of the village.

vyxzme.65: A unique museum in Italy, made of memories of the common people.

1485sl4.85: The civic heart of the country, with a robbian work survived flooding and war.

1gnb3dw.46: The great church that gave the name to the village.

1qlwjjb.59: The shrine to which the most heartfelt feast of the country is linked.
